Subject: Unexplained drop in billed tokens (Nov 25-26)

Hi Lukas —

We're reconciling November usage ahead of our month-end close and noticed a material mismatch between the token counts shown on the Redwood invoice and our internal ingestion metrics for Nov 25-26. Your invoice shows ~2.1M tokens for that window; our internal export shows ~2.7M (roughly a 22% delta).

Attached is a snapshot from our side (quartz-usage-snapshot-20261126.csv) with two request_ids that illustrate the variance. Can you confirm whether Redwood had any telemetry ingestion delays, retention/aggregation windows, or window-alignment issues that could explain this?

We reported a similar gap last quarter and it turned out to be a delayed worker replay — just trying to understand if this is the same class of problem. We need this clarified before finalizing our monthly accounting and AP payment.

Ticket: HUBS-1124 (we opened a support ticket earlier today)

Thanks — appreciate any quick context and whether a provisional credit is possible while you investigate.

Best,
Janelle Park
Director, Finance Ops
Quartz Health

Hypotheses to check (in this order):
- Delayed telemetry ingestion due to worker restart or backlog (events received later and attributed to the wrong billing window)
- Sampling/pruning configured on their account for high-volume streams (unlikely but check configs)
- Metering service rate-limit or duplicate suppression causing token collapse during a window

Marissa: please pull raw ingestion receipts and any replay/retry logs for 2026-11-25 18:00 UTC through 2026-11-26 06:00 UTC. Look for gaps, worker restarts, or unusually late-arriving payloads.
Aditya: please check metering pipeline logs and the windowing logic that assigns events to billing cutoffs (midnight UTC cutoff). If events were ingested after midnight UTC but belong to Nov 25 local time, we may need to reassign.

Customer asked whether a provisional credit is possible while we investigate. If there's a clear ingestion delay, let's prepare a credit estimate.

Thanks — Lukas

Lukas / team — quick summary from initial triage:

What I pulled
- Telemetry receipts for account Quartz Health between 2026-11-25T18:00:00Z and 2026-11-26T06:00:00Z.
- Metering window assignments and the raw tokenized payloads for two request_ids Janelle included: rq_8a3f and rq_bf12.

Findings
- We had a rolling ingress worker restart at 2026-11-25T23:40:12Z (UTC) caused by a failed disk rotation job on that node. The worker came back up ~00:15:00Z but the backlog was handled by the replay queue.
- About 87% of Quartz's events in that span were replayed successfully, but they were processed after the midnight UTC cutoff and consequently got attributed to the Dec 1 billing bucket in our current pipeline (billing cutoffs are midnight UTC). That explains the apparent shortfall on Nov 25-26 on the invoice.
- Attached is a small snippet of the telemetry log showing the worker restart and two of the delayed request lines: redwood-telemetry-snippet.txt

Implications
- This is a window-assignment issue: events were received and metered but assigned to the wrong billing period due to arrival after the UTC cutoff.
- We can reassign these delayed events to the correct Nov billing window for Quartz if they provide written confirmation and we coordinate an adjusted invoice.

Proposed remediation
1) Produce an adjusted usage export that re-attributes delayed events to Nov 25-26 and generate a pro-rated credit for the difference. I've prepared a draft export and a replay plan (replay-plan.md) to ensure the same events are not double-billed.
2) Add a monitoring alert to catch ingress-worker restarts and replay-induced reassignments for high-volume customers (Quartz flagged as "high priority" in our alerting).

Estimate
- Based on the replayed counts the affected tokens ≈ 580,000 (customer-visible delta ~22%). Estimated credit: $4,150 (pre-tax), pending final accounting review.

I'll attach the telemetry snippet and the tentative adjusted export. Marissa
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-telemetry-snippet.txt (log, 6 KB); replay-plan.md (doc, 3 KB)

Subject: Resolution proposal — adjusted Nov usage + provisional credit

Hi Janelle — thanks again for flagging this and for the patience while we investigated.

TL;DR: We confirmed an ingress worker restart on 2026-11-25 that delayed processing of a subset of Quartz Health events. Those delayed events were ingested but assigned to the next billing period due to midnight UTC cutoff behavior.

What we're proposing
- We will re-attribute the delayed events to Nov 25-26 and issue an adjusted usage export (attached: usage-adjusted-202611.csv).
- We propose a provisional credit of $4,150 (pre-tax) for the affected tokens, to be applied to your Dec invoice or issued as a standalone credit memo if you prefer.
- Process: once you confirm in writing we should proceed, we'll: (1) apply the attribution correction in our accounting system, (2) regenerate the invoice, and (3) post the credit. We will not double-bill; replay-plan.md ensures events are idempotent.

Next steps / asks
- Please reply to confirm you'd like us to proceed with the re-attribution and credit.
- If you want the credit applied as of the Dec invoice, we'll schedule that; if you prefer a credit memo now, we can generate it within 2 business days.

References
- HubSpot case: https://app.hubspot.com/cases/RED-12487
- Export (attached) and telemetry snippet (from our logs) are included for your accounting team to reconcile.

Thanks — I'll hold off until I hear back from you.

Best,
